1 November 2021

## Circular to Issuers of SFC-authorised investment-linked assurance schemes (ILAS)

## Enhanced Authorisation Process for New ILAS Applications

1. The purpose of this circular is to introduce an enhanced process for applications for authorisation of new ILAS (Enhanced Process).

## Background

2. The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews and seeks to improve our authorisation process wherever practicable without compromising investor interests and protection. In January 2014, we introduced the 6-month application lapse policy with a view to enhancing the overall efficiency in the authorisation process (Lapse Policy).
3. In performing our regulatory functions, we have regard to, among others, the need to make efficient use of our resources. An authorisation process that is more efficient can also meet the issuers' wish to reduce the 'time to market' of their ILAS products for public offering. As such, the Enhanced Process is introduced to increase the transparency of the authorisation process, promote applicants' compliance and reduce the overall processing time.
4. To achieve this, applicants must provide proper and quality submissions at the time of application and throughout the application process in a timely manner. Applicants must also ensure that their applications are in good order and are accompanied by relevant documents that meet all applicable regulatory requirements.
5. The Enhanced Process only relates to the authorisation process of a new ILAS application under section 104 of the Securities and Futures Ordinance by the SFC. Applicants are still required to obtain a 'no objection' confirmation from the Insurance Authority's (IA) before submission of the new ILAS applications to the SFC (generally referred to as the 'green light' process).

## The Enhanced Process

6. Under the Enhanced Process, a 'two-stream' approach will be adopted by the SFC in processing new ILAS applications.
7. Under the two-stream approach, new ILAS applications will be classified into 'Standard Applications' stream and 'Non-standard Applications' stream. Standard Applications will be fast-tracked with an aim that SFC authorisation (if granted) will be given around 2 to 3 months from the take-up date of the applications. Non-standard Applications will be also processed under an enhanced process with, among others, more discipline in response time with an aim that SFC authorisation will be granted in a more efficient manner under the Lapse Policy.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

8. In general, a new ILAS application will be processed as a Standard Application if the ILAS under application is more simple and standard in nature. Please refer to the Frequently Asked Questions relating to Investment-Linked Assurance Schemes (ILAS FAQs) published on the SFC website for a detailed list of criteria for Standard Applications (see paragraph 16 below).
9. The SFC reserves its right not to take up a new ILAS application which is deemed to be an incomplete application and/or an application that fails to meet the applicable regulatory requirements 1 .
10. Given that Standard Applications are intended to cover less complicated applications, applicants are required to provide proper, complete, and substantive response(s) to the SFC's requisition(s) within 2 months from the date of the first requisition issued by the SFC, failing which the applications may be refused subject to the SFC's right to grant an extension at its sole discretion.
11. To shorten the turnaround time for both Standard Applications and Non-standard Applications, after an application has been taken up by the SFC, time limit(s) will be imposed on the applicants to provide substantive response to properly address SFC's requisition(s) in a timely manner, failing which the applications may be refused subject to the SFC's right to grant an extension at its sole discretion. For further details on the time limit(s) for applicants to respond to SFC's requisitions and related matters, please refer to the ILAS FAQs (see paragraph 16 below).
12.  Authorisation of Standard Applications and Non-standard Applications by the SFC will be granted subject to authorisation conditions which are required to be fulfilled before the authorisation may become effective. Such conditions may include, among others, the receipt of a 'no further comment' confirmation on the application from the IA if not yet obtained.

## Revised Performance Pledges

13. To standardise the performance pledges for all new ILAS applications (i.e. Standard Applications and Non-standard Applications) under the Enhanced Process, the SFC will pledge to (i) take up or refuse to take up a new ILAS application within 5 business days upon receipt of the application; and (ii) issue the first set of response/requisitions to the new ILAS application within 14 business days from the take-up date (Revised Performance Pledges).
14. The Revised Performance Pledges will enable the SFC to conduct a more thorough initial screening and assessment of new ILAS applications.
15. All new ILAS applications that are taken up by the SFC under the Enhanced Process will be subject to the Revised Performance Pledges and the Lapse Policy.

1 As stated in the Information Checklist for Investment-Linked Assurance Schemes (see paragraph 16 below), the SFC reserves the right to return forthwith, without processing, an incomplete or non-compliant application to the extent the Application Form, the Information Checklist and/or the accompanying documents are not properly or fully completed, and/or where negative responses in the Information Checklist are not properly explained, and/or the application is accompanied by documents that do not meet the applicable requirements, not in good order or otherwise not suitable for clearance.

## Updated Information Checklist and ILAS FAQs

16. To implement and provide further guidance on the Enhanced Process, the following documents have been updated and published on the SFC website:
2. (a) an updated Information Checklist for Investment-Linked Assurance Schemes (Information Checklist); and
3. (b) an updated Frequently Asked Questions relating to Investment-Linked Assurance Schemes (please refer to new Quesitons 4A - 4H, 16A and 16B in Section 1 and updated Questions 2, 4 and 9 in Section 1).

## Post-vetting after authorisation

17. Applicants must duly discharge their compliance responsibility and ensure that their SFC-authorised ILAS are in compliance with all applicable requirements including all applicable overarching principles and the eligibility, structural and disclosure requirements under the SFC Handbook for Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds, InvestmentLinked Assurance Schemes and Unlisted Structured Investment Products (including the Code on Investment-Linked Assurance Schemes) at all times.
18. Investor protection is a fundamental regulatory principle. To safeguard investor interests, for SFC-authorised ILAS processed under the Enhanced Process, the SFC will conduct post-vetting to ensure applicable authorisation conditions are complied with. The SFC will, where appropriate, take necessary regulatory action in cases of non-compliance to ensure that investor protection is not compromised.

## General

19. The Enhanced Process shall take effect immediately and apply to all new ILAS applications submitted on or after today.
20. Applicants are welcome to contact SFC to discuss any new ILAS product proposals prior to the submission of the applications to the SFC.
21. The SFC will review the Enhanced Process from time to time and may impose additional requirements/changes where appropriate.
22. Should you wish to clarify any aspects of the Enhanced Process, this circular, the Information Checklist and the ILAS FAQs and/or in case of doubt, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
